metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Alba, Antrim County? Get an honest evaluation of your Antrim Shale interest, no mailbox-offer games, just real numbers.
heroLead: Alba is a small unincorporated crossroads in Antrim County, and small doesn't mean your mineral interest out here gets any less of a straight look than a parcel in Bellaire.
intro: Alba sits in the northern part of Antrim County, farm and forest country that got its share of Antrim Shale drilling during the boom years of the late 1980s and 1990s. If you hold a mineral interest tied to land around Alba, there's a decent chance it's connected to a well that's been in the ground for three decades or more, producing small, steady volumes rather than anything dramatic.

sections.heading: What Antrim Shale production near Alba looks like now
paragraphs: Wells drilled in this part of Antrim County during the boom years are biogenic gas producers, shallow and slow-declining, but decades in, the volumes are a fraction of what they were early on. If your royalty check has shrunk over the years, that's normal for a mature well out here, not a sign something's off with your interest specifically.

We check current operator activity and recent production for the specific section your interest sits in before saying anything about value. A flat number for the Alba area without that step isn't a real evaluation.

sections.heading: Ownership around Alba often runs through farm families
paragraphs: A lot of the mineral rights around Alba trace back to farm land held by the same families for generations, sometimes split off from the surface when a parcel sold, sometimes passed down through heirship without ever being formally divided. If you're getting a small check and don't know exactly what fraction you own, pulling the deed or probate record at the Antrim County register of deeds in Bellaire is the place to start.

faqs.question: Is there active oil and gas production near Alba, MI?
faqs.answer: There's legacy Antrim Shale production in parts of the Alba area tied to wells drilled during the 1980s and 1990s boom, but activity varies section by section. We check your specific parcel before quoting anything.

faqs.question: Why is my royalty check from a well near Alba so small?
faqs.answer: Antrim wells in this part of the county are decades into a long, flat decline. Small, steady volumes at this stage are normal, not a red flag on your interest.

faqs.question: How do I find out exactly what mineral interest I own near Alba?
faqs.answer: Start with the Antrim County register of deeds in Bellaire and pull the deed or probate record showing your ownership, plus your division order if you've received any royalty payments.
